name: Chatbase
tagline: The credit-metered AI chatbot builder that turns a website crawl into a customer-facing support agent in minutes.
tldr: Chatbase is a no-code platform for building custom AI chatbots trained on your own content (website crawls, documents, Q&A) and embedding them on your site, WhatsApp, or other channels.

Pricing is metered in monthly message credits rather than seats or conversations — 50 credits free, 700 on Hobby ($32/mo), 4,000 on Standard ($120/mo), 15,000 on Pro ($400/mo), with heavier models consuming more credits per reply.
Higher tiers unlock voice, telephony, helpdesk features, outbound campaigns, API access, and CRM/helpdesk integrations like Stripe and Zendesk — the Free and Hobby tiers are website-widget-only.
Bootstrapped and founder-led by solo founder Yasser Elsaid (no outside investors), reportedly crossing roughly $9M ARR with a lean ~30-person Toronto-based team as of 2026.

Independent reviews are split: strong marks for ease of setup and fast time-to-launch, but recurring complaints about billing/credit costs, occasional hallucinated answers, and slower support responses.
keyFeatures: Train an agent on crawled website pages, uploaded documents, plain text, or Q&A pairs, with auto-retraining on Standard tier and above
Message-credit billing model where model choice affects cost (e.g. premium models consume more credits per response than standard models)
Voice and telephony support plus a helpdesk/ticketing layer on the Standard plan and up
Native integrations with tools like Stripe, Zendesk, and other business systems on higher tiers
Outbound campaign tooling for proactive messaging, in addition to reactive support replies
API access for embedding chatbot logic into custom applications
Enterprise tier with SSO, white-labeling, audit logs, HIPAA-eligible configuration, and zero data retention options
Analytics dashboards that get more advanced (ticket sourcing, deeper reporting) at the Pro tier

faq.question: How does Chatbase pricing actually work?
faq.answer: Plans are priced monthly and include a pool of message credits rather than a flat conversation cap: Free (50 credits), Hobby $32/mo (700 credits), Standard $120/mo (4,000 credits), Pro $400/mo (15,000 credits). Using a premium model like a top-tier Claude or GPT model can burn multiple credits per single reply, so real usage costs vary with model choice.

faq.question: Can Chatbase read live product prices or stock from my store?
faq.answer: Chatbase trains primarily on crawled/uploaded static content, so live data like stock levels needs to be kept current through re-crawls or connected via integrations/API rather than assumed to update automatically.

faq.question: Does Chatbase support channels beyond the website widget?
faq.answer: Yes — voice and telephony are available starting on the Standard plan, and the platform supports WhatsApp and API-based custom integrations, though the free and Hobby tiers are effectively website-widget-only.

faq.question: Is Chatbase good for enterprise/compliance-heavy teams?
faq.answer: The Enterprise tier adds SSO, audit logs, white-labeling, and a HIPAA-eligible, zero-data-retention configuration, but pricing is custom and requires contacting sales.

faq.question: What do users complain about most?
faq.answer: The most consistent criticisms are around cost scaling with credit consumption, occasional hallucinated answers outside the trained knowledge base, and reports of slower customer support response times on certain plans.

faq.question: Does the reviewer have a relationship with Chatbase?
faq.answer: Yes — disclosed here per this site's methodology: Maxwell Timothy has previously written contributed content for Chatbase. The scoring above uses the same public rubric applied to every other tool on this site.

scorecard.note: Reviewers consistently cite fast time-to-launch — crawl a site, tune the prompt, embed a widget, no code required.
Capable for FAQ-style answers but multiple reviews report hallucinations outside the trained knowledge base, and quality depends heavily on which model tier you're paying for.
Solid on web widget and API; voice/telephony and WhatsApp exist but are gated behind Standard tier and above.
Credit-based billing makes costs unpredictable at scale, and add-ons (extra agents, branding removal, auto-recharge) stack up quickly on top of the sticker price.
Capterra's customer-service score (3.8) trails its ease-of-use score (4.6), and multiple reviewers report slow or unhelpful support interactions.

pricingBreakdown: Chatbase's pricing is a straight message-credit ladder, not a seat count: 50 credits free, 700 for $32/mo on Hobby, 4,000 for $120/mo on Standard, 15,000 for $400/mo on Pro — but that sticker price only tells half the story until you know which model you're pointing at, since a premium model can burn 5 credits on a single reply while a lighter model burns 1. That makes real cost-per-conversation genuinely unpredictable from the pricing page alone, a different failure mode than Wonderchat's resolution-based billing (you pay per successfully-handled conversation, not per model call) or Tidio's Lyro add-on, which starts at $32.50/mo for just 50 AI conversations — a much smaller bucket than $32/mo buys on Chatbase's Hobby tier, but at least it's a number you can actually plan around. The $120/mo Standard tier is the one that matters if you want more than a toy bot, since it's the first tier with voice, telephony, and helpdesk features — that puts it in the same rough price band as Crisp's Essentials plan ($95/mo), except Crisp's $95/mo buys a real omnichannel shared inbox across WhatsApp, Instagram, and email, not a website bot with a ticketing veneer bolted on top.

capabilities.note: This is the entire product — you crawl a site or upload documents, tune a prompt, and the bot answers from that content. It's genuinely fast to get live, but the credit-metering model means the AI's cost and its quality are tied to the same dial: pick a cheaper model to save credits and you're more likely to run into the hallucination complaints that show up repeatedly in independent reviews.

Training sources cover crawled pages, uploaded documents, plain text, and Q&A pairs, with auto-retraining from Standard tier up. The catch worth internalizing: a crawl is a snapshot, not a live feed, so anything that changes often (prices, stock, policies) needs a manual recrawl or an API integration rather than being trusted to update itself.

Outbound campaign tooling shows up on the Standard plan and above, letting the bot proactively message rather than just wait for a question. It's a real feature, but it's bolted onto an AI-agent product rather than being a mature campaign-builder in its own right — don't expect ManyChat-level broadcast sophistication here.

A helpdesk/ticketing layer unlocks at Standard ($120/mo), with ticket-sourcing analytics arriving at Pro. Treat this as a light layer for routing AI-escalated conversations to a human, not a full team-inbox replacement — if a shared inbox is the actual thing you need most, this isn't where Chatbase is strongest.

What ships is a website widget that fronts the AI agent, not a live-chat system built around humans typing back and forth in real time. Independent hands-on reviews specifically flag that Chatbase lacks the built-in live-chat/human-handoff experience that Crisp or Tidio ship by default — the AI is meant to be the front line here, with humans as a fallback, not the other way around.

pros: Very fast to get a working bot live from an existing website with no coding required
Flexible knowledge sources (crawl, documents, text, Q&A) cover most small-to-mid business content needs
Bootstrapped, founder-led company with reportedly strong revenue growth, suggesting product-market fit and staying power
Higher tiers add real depth — voice, telephony, ticketing, and business-system integrations, not just a wider widget
cons: Credit-based pricing makes monthly costs hard to predict, especially once premium models are involved
Multiple independent reviews report hallucinated or made-up answers outside the trained content
Add-ons (extra agents, custom domain, branding removal) meaningfully raise the effective price beyond the sticker plan cost
Customer support quality lags behind product ease-of-use according to third-party review aggregates

bestFor: Solo founders and small teams who want a fast, no-code website support bot
Businesses with well-documented static content (FAQs, policies, guides) suited to crawl-based training
Teams wanting to bolt on voice/telephony or ticketing later without switching platforms
Budget-conscious buyers who can keep message volume within a predictable credit range
verdict: Disclosure up front, same as it says in the FAQ below: I've written contributed content for Chatbase before, so read this knowing I'm not a fully arm's-length reviewer. Here's my honest read anyway — Chatbase earns its popularity on pure setup speed, and pointing it at a website and having a working bot live in minutes is genuinely as easy as it sounds. A solo founder bootstrapping to a reported $9M ARR without outside money says something real about retention, because nobody keeps paying month after month for a bot that quietly embarrasses their brand. What you actually need to watch is the credit-metering model: burning 5 credits per reply on a premium model versus 1 on a lighter model means two businesses sitting on the identical $120/mo Standard plan can end up with wildly different real costs per conversation, and that's not a hypothetical edge case — it's just how the pricing page works. Capterra's 3.8-versus-4.6 gap between support quality and ease-of-use tracks with what reviewers actually describe, so budget for the support experience matching the lower number, not the flashier one. Use it as a fast-to-launch FAQ bot and it'll do exactly what you're paying for; try to make it your full customer-support system of record and you'll start missing what Intercom or Zendesk do with a real shared inbox underneath the AI.
